item.title: Sinn Féin TD accuses Government of delaying cutting taxes on fuel
item.description: A Sinn Féin TD has accused the Government of delaying cutting taxes on fuel. Home heating oil and fuel prices have surged since the war in Iran began; with two tankers targeted off the coast of Iraq this morning. In Ireland, 60% of what is charged on the forecourt is applied by the Government. Advertisement Sinn Féin spokesperson on finance Pearse Doherty says ordinary people are feeling these prices rises on the back of a cost-of-living crisis. item.title: Status yellow snow and ice warning issued for Kerry
item.description: A status yellow snow and ice warning has been issued for 11 counties, including Kerry. It will begin at 9pm and will remain active until 9am tomorrow. Met Éireann says showers may fall as sleet and snow, and could bring about poor visibility and difficult travelling conditions. item.title: Pieta confirms closure of Kerry centre but hopes to secure new base in Tralee
item.description: Suicide prevention charity Pieta is closing its centre in Kerry with administrative staff to lose their jobs. However, Pieta says it’s working to secure a new location in Tralee over the coming months. Its current centre in Moyderwell will close in June. item.title: Kerry Interest On Day Three At Cheltenham
item.description: There is Kerry interest on Day Three of the Cheltenham Festival today. Tralee trainer Tom Cooper will be hoping for a big run from Kerry jockey Jack Kennedy in the opening race. The feature race on today’s seven-race card is the Ryanair Chase, where Jonbon and Banbridge will attempt to dethrone Willie Mullins-trained Fact To File. item.title: Ireland Set For Six Nations Showdown With Scotland
item.description: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell is expected to recall a number of key players for Saturday’s Six Nations clash with Scotland at the Aviva Stadium. Dan Sheehan, Joe McCarthy and Tommy O’Brien are among those tipped to return as Ireland chase a Triple Crown victory. A win would also keep Ireland’s title hopes alive, although they would still require England to defeat France for the championship to fall their way. Advertisement Ireland have recovered well since their opening-round defeat to France.

item.title: Missing Fassbender portrait turns up after going missing in Killarney
item.description: A piece of street art featuring a portrait of actor Michael Fassbender - which went missing in Killarney - has been located. The art work, painted on to an electricity box, had mysteriously vanished from its location near the court house at East Avenue Road. It was created as part of a project funded by Kerry County Council, which also included a likeness of Jessie Buckley. item.title: Cathaoirleach of Kerry County Council to travel New York this weekend for St Patrick’s Day
item.description: The cathaoirleach of Kerry County Council will travel to the United States this weekend to attend a number of St Patrick’s Day engagements. During the visit, councillor Michael Foley, will meet with civic, business and political leaders. He will join the Kerry Association during the St Patrick’s Day Parade on Fifth Avenue on Tuesday. item.title: Kerry Winner As Jack Kennedy Triumphs At Cheltenham
item.description: Kerry jockey Jack Kennedy was back in the winners’ enclosure at the Cheltenham Festival as he guided Wodhooh to victory in the Close Brothers Mares’ Hurdle. The Gordon Elliott-trained six-year-old went off the 5/6 favourite and justified that support with a strong performance up the Cheltenham hill. Wodhooh had already shown impressive form this season and Kennedy produced a confident ride to hold off last year’s runner-up Jade De Grugy in the closing stages. item.title: Timmy Lehane
item.description: Timmy Lehane, Carhan Road, Cahersiveen and formerly of Pembroke Street, Tralee. Died peacefully surrounded by his family in the kind and loving care of Valentia Hospital. Predeceased by his parents Mamie and Florence and his brothers and sisters. He will be deeply missed by his wife Mary, his son Mícheál, daughter in law, Áine, and the three grandchildren he adored, Sadhbh, Ruaidhrí and Donnacha, as well as his nieces, nephews, sisters in law and brothers in law.
